stories.headline: Tsahkna leads trade and digital diplomacy mission to Vietnam, first EU FM to visit since leadership reshuffle
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna conducted a multi-day official visit to Vietnam from April 22–24, meeting Prime Minister Le Minh Hung, Foreign Minister Le Hoai Trung, and Ho Chi Minh City officials. The visit, accompanied by twelve Estonian companies, focused on digital transformation, trade cooperation, and positioning Estonia as a gateway for Vietnamese businesses to the EU; Vietnamese counterparts described Tsahkna as the first EU foreign minister to visit Vietnam since its recent leadership reshuffle.

stories.headline: Pevkur visits Kyiv, signs defense cooperation agreement with Ukraine and commits €110 million in 2026 aid focused on drones
stories.summary: Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur traveled to Kyiv for a three-day visit including the Kyiv Security Forum and an Estonia-Ukraine defence industry forum, where he and Ukrainian Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov signed a letter of intent on defence industry cooperation. Estonia confirmed it will allocate at least 0.25% of GDP (approximately €110 million) to Ukraine in 2026, with priorities on drone procurement, counter-UAV systems, and digital/IT support; the IT Coalition co-led by Estonia crossed €1.4 billion total.

stories.headline: US pauses ammunition deliveries to Estonia for the duration of the Iran conflict, defence minister seeks alternative procurement
stories.summary: Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur disclosed after a phone call with US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth that Washington has paused all ammunition deliveries to Estonia—including HIMARS rockets and Javelin anti-tank weapons—until at least the end of the Iran war, citing US operational requirements. Pevkur said Estonia may need to revisit prior procurement decisions if the pause extends, and indicated Estonia is seeking larger compensatory purchases from the US as well as exploring other suppliers; separately, a new €300 million Turkish-owned ammunition factory (ARCA) was announced for North-Kiviõli.

stories.headline: Estonian officials rebuff Zelensky's claims that Russia is preparing to attack the Baltic states
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna and Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur publicly pushed back on statements by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky suggesting Russia could be preparing to invade the Baltic states, with Tsahkna saying the claims do not match Estonian intelligence assessments and 'do not make cooperation any easier'; Estonian military intelligence chief Colonel Ants Kiviselg also said there are no signs of Russian forces preparing to open a NATO front. EKRE leader Martin Helme separately said Zelensky's rhetoric echoes narratives that Estonia's own political establishment helped create.

stories.headline: Coop Pank reports profit growth for fourth consecutive quarter and enters investment services market
stories.summary: Coop Pank posted a Q1 2026 net profit of €8.3 million, up 5% year-on-year and 15% quarter-on-quarter, maintaining higher capital efficiency than LHV; the bank announced its entry into investment services by hiring a former LHV executive to build a new business line, positioning itself in an increasingly competitive Estonian investment market. The bank also made supervisory board committee changes and disclosed share buyback activity.

stories.headline: Conflicting polls show EKRE hitting 10-year low in one survey while surpassing Reform Party in another
stories.summary: Two separate April polls produced divergent pictures of EKRE's position: Emor showed EKRE at 9%, its lowest in a decade, with Isamaa and Center Party tied at the top; Norstat showed EKRE at 13.7% surpassing the governing Reform Party at 13%, with Isamaa leading at 25.3%. In both surveys, the governing coalition parties (Reform and Eesti 200) held a combined support of roughly 14–15%, well below opposition totals.

stories.headline: President Karis makes official visit to Greece, co-opens Delphi Economic Forum
stories.summary: President Alar Karis made a three-day official visit to Greece where he met President Konstantinos Tassoulas, Parliament speaker Nikitas Kaklamanis, and education minister Sofia Zacharaki; he and Tassoulas jointly opened the Delphi Economic Forum, where Karis argued Europe's competitiveness must be built on its own values rather than copying other economic models. Karis also visited the EU Cybersecurity Agency (ENISA) and called on Estonian-linked clergy and communities in Greece.
